sanity_expectations: a2 = 0 exactly when m1 = m2 (numerator vanishes and every tanh term has zero argument)
sign(a2) = sign(m2 - m1) at fixed other inputs
|a2| < g everywhere in the sampled region
|a2| is monotonically non-increasing in I at fixed m1, m2, R (larger pulley inertia reduces net acceleration magnitude)
|a2| decreases as R decreases at fixed I (through the I/R^2 reflected-mass term)
excitation_report: All 6 additive terms visible above 5*sigma=0.05: dominant (m2-m1)*g/(m1+m2+I/R^2) ~288x; bearing_friction_torque tanh term ~11.8x; cord_mass reflected-mass correction ~22.4x; load-friction Δ vs base ~107x; pulley-mass load-friction Δ ~49.3x; NEW cord-mass-load-friction Δ term ~7.1x (peaks at m1=1.31, m2=1.41, I=0.00375, R=0.063).
role_corrections: a2: O->O (confirmed, explicit dependent variable, not in RHS)
R: V->V (confirmed, sampled independent variable, bounded away from zero to avoid division singularity)
g: P->P (confirmed, fixed physical constant 9.81 m/s^2)
bearing_friction_torque: P->P (confirmed, fixed small load-independent torque)
cord_mass: P->P (confirmed, fixed effective cord mass; raised to 0.15 kg for term visibility)
bearing_load_friction_length: P->P (confirmed, fixed friction moment arm; raised to 0.008 m for new-term visibility)
pulley_mass_inertia_factor: P->P (confirmed, dimensionless, fixed at 2 as for a solid disk)
rationale: Static explicit relation with target a2 not appearing in RHS; four physical inputs (m1, m2, I, R) sampled with linear Sobol-friendly ranges typical of tabletop pulley experiments (masses 0.2-1.5 kg, small pulley radii 3-12 cm, inertia 2e-4 - 1e-2 kg m^2). Parameters set to physically reasonable magnitudes; bearing_load_friction_length and cord_mass tuned upward (still physically plausible) to make the newly added correction term — the cord-mass contribution to bearing radial load — visible above noise. Noise sigma = 0.01 m/s^2 is ~0.3% of the dominant term.
